metric: Calcite optimizer-test pairs from the QED prover, converted from its relational-algebra JSON to SQL, proved equivalent; 2 more are shown different by a counterexample and are not counted in the 373, 15 unknown.
caveats: 375 of QED's 444 cases convert to SQL; 69 use features the conversion cannot reproduce exactly and are not scored (listed with reasons in tests/fixtures/qed/qed_calcite_skipped.jsonl). Overlaps the SQLSolver and R-Bot Calcite sets (not yet deduplicated). Key-based rules were developed with these pairs in view (tuned on test). The outer-join flattening rules (src/kumosql/outer_join_flatten.py) were written with this suite's failing pairs in view (tuned on test). The structural aggregate rules were developed on the failing-tests triage's aggregate cases from this suite (tuned on test). The correlated LATERAL IN rules (quantified_rules.py, #384) were developed with this suite's correlated IN pairs in view (tuned on test). Measured on master fa78ff9 (the pairs that must stay unproven set aside), after the correlated LATERAL IN rules (#384). The 2 pairs shown different by a counterexample stay in the suite as guards (they must never be proved) and are not in the denominator. A branch whose WHERE is the constant FALSE is dropped even when its source is an opaque cut (`ORDER BY .. LIMIT 0`), which proves testSortUnionTranspose3 (smt_equivalence.py `_prune`); this is a general rule, not tuned on a case list.
correctness: 0 false proofs; every proof and the 1 counterexample re-run on 60 random DuckDB databases, half skewed towards the literals
